record.category: managed nebula overlay (private, no public ingress)

free_tier.stated: Get set up in minutes and connect your first 100 devices free, no credit card required.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published; the free unit is devices.; ingress: tcp+udp

record.tooling: Nebula clients plus the vendor's certificate console.
record.chaining: Private path between two rented boxes; no ingress.
record.binding_note: Nothing is metered, so no quota fails at 1 TiB/month. The structure fails: a Nebula overlay has no public address, so an outside peer must be enrolled before it can send a packet.

identity_cost.detail: signup at admin.defined.net, 'no credit card required'.

record.reliability_note: Control plane is hosted and closed; losing it blocks new certificate issuance.
record.confidence_note: A public ingress feature would change the verdict; the page describes private overlay access.

evidence.proved: 'connect your first 100 devices free, no credit card required'; 'Encrypted with the Noise Protocol Framework'

record.notes: Commercial control plane for open-source Nebula. The aggregator is explicit that this is private overlay access rather than public-URL ingress.

extras.wg_detail: The data plane is Nebula, which is its own protocol on UDP 4242, not WireGuard. No .conf export exists; the overlay certificate is issued by the hosted control plane.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published; the free unit is devices.
extras.transit_note: Peer-to-peer Nebula; the hosted plane issues certificates.
